title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-04-08
content:
Weekly serving-runtime update (kernel work, KV cache, batching) - 2026-04-08

Attendees / contributors: Aisha (owner), Marco, Lena, Devon, Priya (notes), SRE: Omar (summary review)

Purpose: quick sync for kernel-level optimizations, KV cache behavior changes, batching policy tweaks, and rollout plan for the upcoming 2026Q2 perf release. This is a working doc - rough notes, open questions, and action items at the bottom.

High-level summary:
- Kernel selection improvements (fast-path dispatch) landed in staging branch; microbenchmarks show median token latency down ~8-12% for 16k-seq on A100-like profiles. Still seeing tail variance on mixed-size requests.
- KV cache LRU eviction fix merged; observed ~3-5% cost reduction in synthetic chat workload due to higher reuse, but some customers report cache churn on multi-tenant Dedicated pools. Investigating routing and tenant isolation interactions.
- Batching changes: new adaptive batcher prototype (per-model shape-based batching) reduced batching overhead for short-chat workloads and improved p99 latency under 75th percentile throughput. Need more load testing under burst scenarios.

Deep dives
1) Kernel work
- What landed: fast-path kernel dispatch (PR #1187) that picks a shorter kernel sequence for common attention patterns (causal + fixed prompt prefix). This avoids the expensive fused-kernel fallback path for common cases.
- Benchmarks: internal microbenchmarks (model: rw-7b-v2-ish) on p4d equivalents.
  - mean token latency: -9%
  - median token latency: -11%
  - p99 token latency: -4% (still dominated by GC/KV miss spikes)
- Observed regressions: a small class of long-context prompt permutations hit a suboptimal kernel due to our shape-hash collision; tracked as JIRA INF-3500. Lena is debugging the hash function and will propose a fix next week.
- Next: add more deterministic kernel selection logging (event will include model, seq_len, shape_hash, chosen_kernel) so we can correlate tails to selection. Targeting rollout gating: must have <1% degraded-requests vs canary.

2) KV cache
- LRU eviction fix details: eviction logic previously allowed simultaneous eviction markers across multiple shards which could cause premature invalidation for re-used prefixes. Fix consolidates markers via a global sequence-numbered tombstone.
- Observed impact: in local replay tests with customer A's chat traces we saw a 3.4% token compute reduction and 2.1% latency improvement. However in multi-tenant Dedicated testing, tenant A saw improvements while tenant B saw slightly higher cache churn - hypothesis: uneven routing caused rapid tenant switching across the same GPU causing cache pollution.
- Action: Priya and Marco to run a tenant-isolation replay test with pinned routing for 48h and compare cache hit curves. Also to test with sticky-routing enabled (JIRA INF-3480).
- Open bug: cache tombstone size grows under heavy long-context workloads and increases memory pressure. Tracked as INF-3495; proposed mitigations: tombstone compaction and heuristics to keep only N recent tombstones per shard.

3) Batching
- Adaptive batcher prototype: groups requests by (model, dtype, remaining_decode_len_bucket) and uses a short (5-20ms) coalescing window for short sequences and a longer window for long sequences. This hybrid approach reduces average batching overhead while keeping tail latency bounded for long requests.
- Results from spike test (simulated PLG chat traffic):
  - avg throughput: +6%
  - avg latency (tokens): -7%
  - p95 latency: -9% (improvement), p99: mixed depending on burst pattern
- Problem: under very bursty traffic with many small short-lived connections, the coalescing window increases p99 unless we impose a hard cap on max batch wait time. Proposed: enforce max_wait_ms=50 for interactive tiers and 150ms for background tiers.
- Integrations: batching changes require sync with router team (INF-3522) because grouping by remaining_decode_len_bucket must be signalled in route metadata. Talking to Alex on Friday to align APIs.

Operational notes / metrics observed this week
- Canary clusters (staging) saw request success rate 99.98% during kernel dispatch rollout. No widespread OOMs.
- KV cache hit-rate improved from 61% -> 64% in replay tests; Dedicated test cluster had higher variance: mean 62% +- 6%.
- Cost estimate: if production sees 3% compute reduction, expected monthly infra savings ~5-7% on inference spend for customers using rw-7b family. Need formal econ analysis from finance for Q2 deck.

Customer reports / support flags
- CS reported a Dedicated customer on EMEA region saw occasional spike in latency and kv-cache evictions correlated with tenant scaling events. Support ticket: CS-1987. Prioritized for investigation.
- Also received feedback from Solutions Eng that the new kernel selection logs are helpful; request to add correlation id to logs so they can tie to trace IDs (action item below).

Risks / blockers
- Kernel selection hash collisions (INF-3500) causing degraded kernel choices for some long-context shapes. Blocker for wide rollout.
- Tombstone growth causing memory pressure (INF-3495). Need compaction before rollout to Dedicated.
- API contract needed for router to share remaining_decode_len_bucket - blocking batching integration until aligned (INF-3522).

Meeting / standup notes
- 2026-04-07 standup: quick sync, agreed to hold a 1hr cross-team call next Monday with Router, SRE, and Solutions Eng to walk deployment plan. Action: Aisha to send invite and agenda.
- Kernel sync (2026-04-06): Lena presented hashing diagnostic; plan to land deterministic logging and a hash fix by 2026-04-13.
- KV cache deep dive (2026-04-02): Priya showed replay results; decided to run pinned routing test for 48h starting 2026-04-09.

Action items (owners, target dates)
- Lena: implement hash function fix + unit tests, target 2026-04-13 (INF-3500).
- Priya & Marco: run tenant-pinned replay (48h) and share hit-rate graphs, target 2026-04-10.
- Aisha: schedule cross-team deployment sync (Router, SRE, Solutions Eng) for 2026-04-13 and send deployment checklist.
- Devon: add deterministic kernel-selection logging (shape_hash + chosen_kernel + trace_id), PR by 2026-04-12 (also add sampling to avoid log spike).
- Marco: run long-burst spike test for adaptive batcher with sticky-routing on/off, report by 2026-04-14.
- Omar (SRE): validate tombstone compaction plan under heavy mem scenarios and recommend safe default thresholds by 2026-04-15.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add a short doc on how remaining_decode_len_bucket is computed so Router and SDK teams can reason about grouping.
- Prep a small benchmark artifact (runbook) for Solutions Eng to reproduce the microbenchmarks (model configs, input corpus, hardware targets).

Unresolved questions
- What is the right max_wait_ms tradeoff for PLG interactive tier? current heuristics look reasonable but need product input.
- If tombstone compaction reduces correctness risk, does it change the eviction semantics? Need to document.

Appendix - quick links
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1187
- KV cache tickets: JIRA INF-3495, INF-3480
- Batcher design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Batcher+Design

If anything needs to be added, paste notes here. This doc will be updated as we make progress and after the cross-team sync on 2026-04-13.
